title: How Do LLMs Understand Legal Philosophy? Diagnosing Legal-Philosophical Reasoning in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.19427v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Legal reasoning is a fundamental capability for large language models (LLMs) to complete legal AI tasks such as legal judgment prediction. In legal practice, this reasoning is shaped by legal philosophy: a judge's view of the nature and sources of law guides how legal materials are interpreted and applied, so judges working from the same statutes and precedents can reach different judgments. Existing research has largely overlooked whether LLMs can understand legal philosophy and apply it in legal reasoning, an ability we call \textit{legal-philosophical reasoning}. To fill this gap, we introduce LePhilBench, a benchmark for evaluating the legal-philosophical reasoning of LLMs that comprises two benchmarking tasks and a dataset. The two tasks evaluate how well LLMs understand legal philosophy and how well they apply it in legal reasoning, respectively. The dataset is manually and meticulously constructed. translated_title: 大语言模型如何理解法律哲学？诊断大语言模型中的法律哲学推理
translated_abstract: 法律推理是大语言模型（LLM）完成法律判断预测等法律AI任务的一项基础能力。在法律实践中，这种推理受到法律哲学的影响：法官对法律的本质和法律渊源的看法决定了其如何解释和适用法律材料，因此面对相同法条和判例的法官可能得出不同的判决。现有研究在很大程度上忽视了大语言模型能否理解法律哲学并将其运用于法律推理，我们将这种能力称为“法律哲学推理”。为填补这一空白，我们提出了LePhilBench，一个用于评估大语言模型法律哲学推理能力的基准，它包含两个基准测试任务和一个数据集。这两个任务分别评估大语言模型对法律哲学的理解程度，以及将法律哲学运用于法律推理的程度。该数据集经过人工精心构建，其测试集包含220个美国最高……（摘要内容在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出LePhilBench基准，通过“理解法律哲学”与“应用法律哲学”两项任务及人工精心构建的数据集，首次系统评估了大语言模型的法律哲学推理能力。
